LAUNCH.TITLE: We got tired of fake Claude. So we built {appName}.
LAUNCH.DESCRIPTION: Outages every other week. Premium models silently swapped for cheap clones. We snapped, shipped our own router, and made it paranoid about both. Here is the launch story.
LAUNCH.AUTHOR: {appName} team
LAUNCH.INTRO: The cheap AI API market has two problems. Providers go down a lot, and some of them quietly forward your request to a weaker model while still charging you for the flagship. {appName} is built to fix both.
LAUNCH.P_UPTIME: Cheap upstreams are cheap for a reason. They rate-limit, throttle, and drop connections under load. When one degrades, {appName} routes the same request to another healthy provider serving the same model, automatically. Your application doesn't see the outage. You don't rewrite your code. You just keep shipping.
LAUNCH.H_AUTHENTIC: Every model is the real model
LAUNCH.P_AUTHENTIC: Not every gateway serves what it advertises. Some forward premium model names to cheaper substitutes and hope you don't notice. {appName} validates authenticity on every model we list: we probe identity and behavior end to end, and if a provider lies, we cut them. When you call Claude, you get Claude. When you call GPT, you get GPT.
LAUNCH.H_HARNESS: Works in the terminals you actually use
LAUNCH.P_HARNESS: A model is only useful if it works in your tools. We test every model end to end for HTTP completion, streaming, and tool calling. Those three capabilities are what AI terminal harnesses depend on. If a model is in our catalog, it works in Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and any OpenAI-compatible client. No surprise 'streaming not supported' failures mid-session.
LAUNCH.P_NEXT: We ship weekly. Expect more models, tighter health signals driving smarter fallbacks, richer cost and latency dashboards, and deeper integrations with the terminals and IDEs you already live in.
LAUNCH.CTA: Ready to try it? <register>Grab an API key</register> or <models>browse the model catalog</models>.

AGENT_READY.TITLE: We pointed Cloudflare's agent scanner at our site. It came back 100/100.
AGENT_READY.DESCRIPTION: Cloudflare just shipped a scanner that grades how ready your site is for AI agents. We hit a perfect 100/100 and the top Level 5 rating. Here is exactly what it checks and why most sites fail.
AGENT_READY.AUTHOR: {appName} team
AGENT_READY.INTRO: An AI agent walks up to your domain. Can it figure out who you are, what you offer, how to talk to you, and how to pay you? That is the question Cloudflare's Is Your Site Agent-Ready scanner tries to answer. We pointed it at {appDomain} and got back a perfect 100/100 with the top-tier Level 5 Agent-Native rating.
AGENT_READY.P_SCORE: Five categories, all green. Discoverability 3/3, Content 1/1, Bot Access Control 3/3, API/Auth/MCP/Skill Discovery 7/7, and the optional Commerce category passing as well. As far as the scanner is concerned, every emerging agent standard it knows how to look for is in place on {appDomain}.
AGENT_READY.IMG_ALT: Is Your Site Agent-Ready report card showing {appDomain} with a 100 score and Level 5 Agent-Native badge
AGENT_READY.H_WHAT: What Is Your Site Agent-Ready actually checks
AGENT_READY.P_WHAT: It is a free Cloudflare scanner that hits your domain and looks for the technical signals AI agents use to discover and interact with a site. Think of it as a checklist: robots.txt, sitemap, link headers, content-type negotiation for markdown, AI bot rules, MCP server cards, agent skill manifests, OAuth discovery documents, x402 payment headers, and several emerging commerce protocols. Each check is one small HTTP call against a well-known path or header.
AGENT_READY.P_CATEGORIES: Discoverability covers robotsTxt (a robots.txt that parses), sitemap (a sitemap.xml the scanner can fetch), and linkHeaders (Link: headers that point at machine-readable manifests). Content covers markdownNegotiation (whether the site responds with markdown when an agent asks for it). Bot Access Control covers robotsTxtAiRules (explicit AI-agent allow/deny rules), contentSignals (Cloudflare's content-signals format) and webBotAuth (signed bot identity). API/Auth/MCP/Skill Discovery covers apiCatalog (a discoverable API listing), oauthDiscovery and oauthProtectedResource (RFC 9728 OAuth metadata), mcpServerCard (a Model Context Protocol server descriptor), a2aAgentCard (Google's Agent-to-Agent card), agentSkills (declared skill list) and webMcp (HTTP-bound MCP). Commerce covers x402 (the HTTP 402 payment standard), mpp, ucp and acp (three competing autonomous-commerce drafts). {appDomain} answers correctly on all of them.
AGENT_READY.P_STUBS: These checks are simple stubs. The scanner mostly verifies that a well-known URL exists, returns a 200, and contains the right top-level shape. It does not run a real OAuth flow, it does not actually invoke an MCP tool, it does not settle an x402 payment. A green tick means the door is unlocked, not that the room behind it is finished. Anyone who depends on a protocol in production should still do their own end-to-end verification: round-trip the OAuth flow, call the MCP tool from a real client, run an x402 payment all the way to settlement. The score is a great signal that the surface area is in place. It is not a substitute for protocol-level conformance testing.
AGENT_READY.H_TRY: Run it on your own site
AGENT_READY.P_TRY: If you build anything that AI agents might one day touch, the scanner is genuinely worth a minute of your time. It surfaces a long list of small standards in one view and tells you exactly which well-known paths are missing or malformed. We use it as a regression check whenever we ship anything that touches discovery, auth, or commerce surfaces.
AGENT_READY.CTA: Scan your site at <scanner>isitagentready.com</scanner>, or if you came here for {appName}, <register>grab an API key</register> and start routing.

FAQ.A1: You pay per token consumed. Each model has its own input, output and cache rate, billed from your account credit. There is no monthly subscription required for Pay As You Go.
FAQ.A2: No. Pay As You Go is fully self-serve, top up once and consume any model. Subscriptions give better value (up to 1.75x credit multiplier) if your usage is predictable.
FAQ.Q3: Is the API compatible with OpenAI?
FAQ.A3: Yes. {appName} exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for chat completions, plus Anthropic and Gemini compatible endpoints. Point any OpenAI SDK at our base URL and use your {appName} API key.
FAQ.A4: Every plan includes access to all supported models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek and more). We do not gate models by tier.
FAQ.Q5: What happens if a provider fails?
FAQ.A5: {appName} routes requests across multiple providers with automatic failover. If one provider is rate-limited or down, we retry against the next healthy upstream transparently.
FAQ.A6: Unused prepaid credit is refundable for 30 days from purchase. Contact {supportEmail} for refund requests.
FAQ.Q7: Can I use this with SillyTavern, Janitor.AI, Chub, or RisuAI?
FAQ.A7: Yes. Every plan works as a custom OpenAI-compatible source in any major roleplay client. SillyTavern, Janitor.AI, RisuAI, and Chub each have a setup guide in the docs.
FAQ.Q8: How long can my conversations or character history be?
FAQ.A8: {appName} supports the full context window of every model, up to 1M tokens on Gemini and 200k on Claude. Long roleplays and long codebases both work.

SILLYTAVERN.TITLE: SillyTavern Integration Guide
SILLYTAVERN.SUBTITLE: Connect {appName} to SillyTavern through the Custom OpenAI-compatible chat completion source.
SILLYTAVERN.INTRO_DESC: SillyTavern is a self-hosted roleplay and character chat frontend for large language models. It runs locally, stores characters and chats on your own machine, and supports any OpenAI-compatible API as its chat completion source.
SILLYTAVERN.OVERVIEW_DESC: SillyTavern talks to {appName} through the Chat Completion source. You paste the base URL, your API key, and pick a model from the auto-populated dropdown. No proxy server, no reverse tunnel, no extra setup.
SILLYTAVERN.QUICK_CONFIG_DESC: Copy these three values into the Custom (OpenAI-compatible) source fields in SillyTavern.
SILLYTAVERN.QUICK_CONFIG_NOTE: Paste the base URL only. SillyTavern appends `/chat/completions` automatically. Adding it yourself will cause a 400 error.
SILLYTAVERN.STEP_1_DESC: In SillyTavern, click the plug icon at the top to open the API Connections panel.
SILLYTAVERN.STEP_2_DESC: Set the API type to Chat Completion.
SILLYTAVERN.STEP_3_DESC: In the Chat Completion Source dropdown, choose Custom (OpenAI-compatible).
SILLYTAVERN.STEP_4_DESC: Enter {appName}'s base URL ending in `/v1`. Do not add `/chat/completions`.
SILLYTAVERN.STEP_5_DESC: Paste your {appName} API key into the Custom API Key field.
SILLYTAVERN.STEP_6_DESC: Click Connect. The Model dropdown auto-populates from {appName}'s model list; pick the one you want.
SILLYTAVERN.STEP_7_DESC: If SillyTavern still shows a warning banner even though messages go through, enable Bypass API Status Check.
SILLYTAVERN.MODELS_DROPDOWN_DESC: SillyTavern calls `GET /v1/models` on your base URL to populate the model picker. {appName} exposes this endpoint, so the dropdown fills automatically. If it ever comes up empty, fall back to the Custom Model ID text field and type the model name yourself.
SILLYTAVERN.TS_1_DESC: You appended `/chat/completions` to the URL. Remove it; the base URL must end at `/v1`.
SILLYTAVERN.TS_2_DESC: The connection failed. Re-check the base URL, then toggle Bypass API Status Check so SillyTavern stops short-circuiting the list.
SILLYTAVERN.TS_3_DESC: The API key is expired or mistyped. Generate a new one from your {appName} dashboard and paste it without leading or trailing spaces.
SILLYTAVERN.TS_4_DESC: You hit the rate limit on your current plan. Wait a minute or upgrade the plan on the {appName} billing page.
SILLYTAVERN.TS_5_DESC: Your system clock is off. Sync it and retry; SillyTavern uses the system trust store.
SILLYTAVERN.TS_6_DESC: Disable Streaming in the generation settings to confirm the issue is on the stream side, then re-enable it. Corporate proxies that strip the `data:` prefix can also cause this.
SILLYTAVERN.CTA_DESC: Get your {appName} API key and start running SillyTavern against every model we support.

META.TITLE: Janitor.AI Integration Guide | {appName}
META.DESCRIPTION: Connect Janitor.AI to {appName} as a custom proxy. Includes the exact full-path URL Janitor expects and the browser-refresh step that most guides forget.
META.KEYWORDS: Janitor AI, Janitor proxy, Janitor API, {appName} Janitor, roleplay proxy, OpenAI-compatible roleplay, Janitor custom proxy URL

JANITOR_AI.TITLE: Janitor.AI Integration Guide
JANITOR_AI.SUBTITLE: Connect {appName} to Janitor.AI as a custom proxy with the exact URL format Janitor's API Settings panel expects.
JANITOR_AI.INTRO_DESC: Janitor.AI is a browser-based character chat platform. It ships a built-in free model and lets you add any OpenAI-compatible proxy for unlimited access. {appName} plugs in at the API Settings panel.
JANITOR_AI.OVERVIEW_DESC: Janitor.AI calls your proxy at the FULL `/v1/chat/completions` URL. You paste that URL, your API key, and the model name into a configuration, hit Save, then hard-refresh the browser for the configuration to activate.
JANITOR_AI.QUICK_CONFIG_DESC: Copy these three values into the Add Configuration panel in Janitor.AI.
JANITOR_AI.QUICK_CONFIG_NOTE: Paste the full URL ending in `/v1/chat/completions`, not just the base URL. If Janitor shows an 'Add /chat/completions to URL' checkbox, leave it OFF.
JANITOR_AI.WARN_REFRESH_DESC: After you click Save Settings, Janitor.AI will not activate the new proxy until the browser reloads. Press Ctrl+Shift+R (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+Shift+R (macOS) before sending a test message. This is the single most common reason a freshly saved proxy appears broken.
JANITOR_AI.STEP_1_DESC: Start any chat and click the gear icon at the top-right of the chat view.
JANITOR_AI.STEP_2_DESC: Select API Settings, then click Add Configuration.
JANITOR_AI.STEP_3_DESC: Config Name (anything), Model Name (from {appName}'s models page), Proxy URL (the full `/v1/chat/completions` URL), API Key.
JANITOR_AI.STEP_4_DESC: Save the configuration into the list of available proxies.
JANITOR_AI.STEP_6_DESC: Press Ctrl+Shift+R or Cmd+Shift+R. The proxy only activates after a full page reload.
JANITOR_AI.REFRESH_SAVE_DESC: Janitor.AI caches the proxy map at page load. Saving rewrites local storage but the already-loaded app still holds the old map. The hard-refresh forces Janitor to re-read the fresh configuration.
JANITOR_AI.KEY_INVISIBILITY_DESC: Janitor.AI masks the API key field after save; you cannot copy it back out. Store the key in a password manager before you paste it, so rotation or a second browser profile does not require a new key generation.
JANITOR_AI.TS_1_TITLE: A 'Free tier limit reached' banner appears.
JANITOR_AI.TS_1_DESC: That banner is Janitor's built-in tier, not {appName}. Switch the chat to your saved proxy configuration in the model dropdown at the top of the chat.
JANITOR_AI.TS_2_TITLE: Proxy does not respond after save.
JANITOR_AI.TS_2_DESC: You did not hard-refresh. Press Ctrl+Shift+R or Cmd+Shift+R and retry.
JANITOR_AI.TS_3_DESC: The Proxy URL is missing the `/v1/chat/completions` suffix. Re-open the configuration and paste the full URL.
JANITOR_AI.TS_4_DESC: Wrong API key. Janitor hid the old key, so delete the configuration and recreate it with a fresh key from your password manager or the {appName} dashboard.
JANITOR_AI.TS_5_DESC: Increase Max Tokens in Janitor's Generation Settings. This is not a proxy issue; it is a Janitor-side output limit.
JANITOR_AI.TS_6_TITLE: Wrong model replies, or a 'model not found' error.
JANITOR_AI.TS_6_DESC: The Model Name field must match a model ID exactly. Copy-paste from {appName}'s models page rather than retyping.
JANITOR_AI.CTA_DESC: Get your {appName} API key and run Janitor.AI against every model we support.

META.TITLE: RisuAI Integration Guide | {appName}
META.DESCRIPTION: Connect RisuAI to {appName} via Custom Models. Includes the critical step of unchecking Autofill Request URL, the #1 support issue for RisuAI proxy setups.
META.KEYWORDS: RisuAI, RisuAI proxy, RisuAI custom endpoint, {appName} RisuAI, roleplay AI proxy, Autofill Request URL, RisuAI OpenAI-compatible

RISUAI.TITLE: RisuAI Integration Guide
RISUAI.SUBTITLE: Connect {appName} to RisuAI through the Custom Models option in Advanced Settings.
RISUAI.INTRO_DESC: RisuAI is a local-first roleplay chat frontend that runs in the browser or as a desktop app. It supports any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with configuration stored in browser local storage.
RISUAI.INTRO_WIKI_NOTE: The official RisuAI wiki is behind the current UI. Steps below reflect RisuAI as of 2026-04.
RISUAI.OVERVIEW_DESC: RisuAI's Custom Models slot lets you paste a Request URL, API key, and model ID. The gotcha is a toggle called Autofill Request URL: when it is on, RisuAI rewrites the URL you paste, which silently breaks the connection.
RISUAI.WARN_AUTOFILL_TITLE: Uncheck Autofill Request URL before pasting
RISUAI.WARN_AUTOFILL_DESC: If Autofill Request URL is on, RisuAI rewrites whatever URL you paste into its own default format, which breaks the connection with no error. Uncheck this toggle BEFORE you paste the Request URL. This is the single most common reason a RisuAI + custom proxy setup fails.
RISUAI.QUICK_CONFIG_DESC: Copy these three values into the Custom Models fields in RisuAI's Advanced Settings.
RISUAI.QUICK_CONFIG_NOTE: Paste the full URL ending in `/v1/chat/completions`. RisuAI has no model dropdown in Custom Models mode; the Model ID is a manual text field.
RISUAI.STEP_1_DESC: In RisuAI, open Settings, then Advanced Settings.
RISUAI.STEP_2_DESC: Click the Chat Bot model selector, scroll to the bottom of the model list, and choose Custom Models.
RISUAI.STEP_3_DESC: This toggle must be OFF before you paste anything. See the critical warning above.
RISUAI.STEP_4_DESC: Paste the full URL ending in `/v1/chat/completions`.
RISUAI.STEP_5_DESC: Paste your {appName} API key into the API Key field. Some RisuAI builds label this field Authorization; use that field if the API Key field does not appear.
RISUAI.STEP_6_DESC: Type or paste the exact model name from {appName}'s models page.
RISUAI.STEP_7_DESC: Close the settings panel; RisuAI writes configuration to local storage.
RISUAI.STEP_8_DESC: Open any chat and send a test message to verify the response.
RISUAI.AUTOFILL_WARNING_DETAIL_DESC: Autofill Request URL was added to prevent typos against named preset providers. For Custom Models, it becomes a foot-gun: RisuAI rewrites your custom URL to a default that does not point at us. If a RisuAI update flips this toggle back on, redo step 3 before debugging anything else.
RISUAI.AUX_MODEL_DESC: RisuAI uses a second model slot for translation, summary, and name-guessing tasks. Repeat steps 2 through 7 for the Auxiliary Model selector, using the same {appName} URL and key.
RISUAI.TS_1_DESC: Autofill Request URL was on when you pasted; RisuAI rewrote the URL. Uncheck the toggle and re-paste the Request URL.
RISUAI.TS_2_DESC: A RisuAI update can re-enable Autofill Request URL silently. Open Custom Models and confirm it is still off.
RISUAI.TS_3_DESC: RisuAI builds sometimes expose both API Key and Authorization fields; only one is read depending on version. Move your key to the other field and retry.
RISUAI.TS_4_DESC: The Model ID must match a model name exactly. Copy-paste from {appName}'s models page; do not retype.
RISUAI.TS_5_TITLE: Translation or summary feature is broken.
RISUAI.TS_5_DESC: The Auxiliary Model is unconfigured. Repeat setup for the Auxiliary Model slot.
RISUAI.TS_6_TITLE: Streaming output is chunked or missing pieces.
RISUAI.TS_6_DESC: RisuAI's SSE parser expects plain `data:` events. A corporate proxy stripping the prefix will produce garbled streaming. Test on a non-corporate network if available.
RISUAI.TS_7_DESC: RisuAI stores configuration in browser local storage, which some privacy modes clear. Export your config to a file from Settings for backup.
RISUAI.CTA_DESC: Get your {appName} API key and run RisuAI against every model we support.

CHUB.TITLE: Chub / Venus Integration Guide
CHUB.SUBTITLE: Connect {appName} to Chub.ai (Venus) through the Secrets panel's Reverse proxy option.
CHUB.INTRO_DESC: Chub.ai (formerly Venus) is a browser-based character chat platform with a 60,000-character library. It connects to OpenAI-compatible endpoints through its Secrets panel.
CHUB.OVERVIEW_DESC: Chub's Secrets panel accepts a full `/v1/chat/completions` URL plus your API key. A Check your proxy button verifies the connection before you pick a model in Prompt Structure.
CHUB.TRUST_DESC: Chub's UI warns about 'reverse proxies created by unauthorized third parties.' That warning targets community-run relays. {appName} is a first-party API relay operated by the infrastructure owner, analogous to OpenRouter. Your API key, usage logs, and billing live on {appName} directly.
CHUB.QUICK_CONFIG_DESC: Copy these two values into the Reverse proxy fields in Chub's Secrets panel.
CHUB.QUICK_CONFIG_NOTE: Paste the full URL ending in `/v1/chat/completions`. Chub expects the full path; do not paste only the base URL.
CHUB.STEP_1_DESC: Click the hamburger menu at the top-right of Chub, then select Secrets.
CHUB.STEP_2_DESC: Click the OpenAI section to expand it.
CHUB.STEP_3_DESC: The Reverse proxy subsection contains the URL and Key fields plus the Check your proxy button.
CHUB.STEP_4_DESC: URL ends in `/v1/chat/completions`. Key is your {appName} API key.
CHUB.STEP_5_DESC: Wait for the green confirmation. If it fails, recheck the URL and re-paste the key.
CHUB.STEP_6_DESC: Return to the hamburger menu, select Configuration, then Prompt Structure.
CHUB.STEP_7_DESC: Set the API dropdown to OpenAI, then select your target model from the model dropdown.
CHUB.PICK_MODEL_TITLE: The model dropdown needs a passing proxy check
CHUB.PICK_MODEL_DESC: Chub only populates the model dropdown in Prompt Structure after the proxy check succeeds. If the dropdown is empty, go back and re-run Check your proxy in Secrets → OpenAI → Reverse proxy.
CHUB.WARN_KEY_INVISIBLE_DESC: Chub masks the API key after save. You cannot copy it back out. Save the key in a password manager before pasting so rotation or a second browser profile does not require a new key.
CHUB.TS_1_DESC: URL is wrong. It must end in `/v1/chat/completions`; the base URL alone will not pass.
CHUB.TS_2_DESC: The proxy check has not passed yet. Re-run step 5 and wait for the green state.
CHUB.TS_3_DESC: Prompt Structure has the wrong API selected. Open Configuration → Prompt Structure and switch the API dropdown to OpenAI.
CHUB.TS_4_DESC: Your API key was rotated or typo'd. Generate a new key at your {appName} dashboard, then re-paste into Reverse proxy.
CHUB.TS_5_DESC: Lower the max context in Prompt Structure, or pick a model with a larger context on {appName}'s models page.
CHUB.TS_6_TITLE: After reload the proxy check says pass but messages fail.
CHUB.TS_6_DESC: Chub caches the proxy-check state across sessions. Press Check your proxy once on a new session to force a fresh check.
CHUB.CTA_DESC: Get your {appName} API key and run Chub / Venus against every model we support.

AGENT_CARD.DESCRIPTION: Unified AI model gateway. One OpenAI-compatible endpoint for every major model (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and more) with automatic failover and intelligent routing.
AGENT_CARD.AUTH_DESCRIPTION: Two options. (1) {appName} API key: generate in the dashboard and send as Authorization: Bearer sk-... . (2) OAuth 2.1 + PKCE for agents acting on behalf of a signed-in user; the agent can then mint its own API key via the tokens:write scope. Discover the authorization server at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server on the API origin and the resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource on this origin.

SKILLS.CHAT_COMPLETION_DESCRIPTION: OpenAI-compatible chat completion across every supported model. Supports streaming, tool calls, and vision where the underlying model does.
SKILLS.IMAGE_GENERATION_DESCRIPTION: Generate images through supported image models.
SKILLS.VIDEO_GENERATION_DESCRIPTION: Generate videos through supported video models, including async task polling for long-running renders.
SKILLS.AUDIO_DESCRIPTION: Text-to-speech, speech-to-text transcription, and audio understanding through supported audio models.
SKILLS.EMBEDDINGS_DESCRIPTION: Text embedding generation through supported embedding models.
SKILLS.MODEL_CATALOG_DESCRIPTION: List all available models with live pricing. Useful for dynamic model selection based on cost, context window, or capability.

AGENT_SKILLS.ROUTE_CHAT: Call an OpenAI-compatible chat completion against any model from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and more through a single endpoint. Use when the user wants to compare models, needs automatic failover between providers, or wants one billing surface for multiple LLM providers.
AGENT_SKILLS.BROWSE_CATALOG: Discover available AI models with live pricing across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, and other providers. Use when the user needs to pick a model by cost, context window, or capability before calling the API.

MCP.SERVER_DESCRIPTION: In-browser AI model router. Tools are registered via WebMCP on the site homepage using navigator.modelContext. Visit the homepage and call the tools from a WebMCP-capable client.
MCP.WEBMCP_BUNDLE_DESCRIPTION: In-browser tools registered via navigator.modelContext on the {appName} homepage. Load the homepage in a WebMCP-capable client to access tools.
